hypothesis: The cross-asset strategy presented to operators as HT-Breakout may retain an after-cost edge on SOL under its unchanged five-minute breakout-onset contract.
decision: Keep the unchanged SOL HT-Breakout transfer rejected for a future profile. The current v25 SOL lifecycle remains owned by its frozen live plan until it resolves, but one open winner cannot override the negative 365-day transfer, failed tuned holdout, and negative prior L2-aligned forward challenger.
falsifier: Reopen this exact-route decision after a prospectively declared sample contains at least 20 independently spaced resolved SOL HT-Breakout live lifecycles across at least 30 calendar days, remains net positive with profit factor above 1.0 after actual fees and funding, and does not derive more than half of gross profit from one trade. That evidence would trigger review, not automatic promotion.
limitations: The operator-facing name is HT-Breakout, while the legacy strategy_id is retained for checkpoint and ledger compatibility.
The final 60-day historical block had already been opened and is descriptive rather than newly sealed.
The tuned development winner was selected post hoc and failed its opened final block.
The L2-aligned forward challenger used recorded BBO simulation rather than private live fills, queue position, or realized slippage.
The active v25 SOL lifecycle was still open at the immutable prefix and contributes no resolved performance evidence.
This revision records a future-profile research decision only; it cannot stop, pause, filter, resize, or otherwise mutate the running v25 lifecycle.
